en: Free Trade Zone - Areas within a country where goods can be imported, handled, and re-exported without paying customs duties.
Frontier Markets - Less advanced capital markets from the developing world.
Geo-economics - The intersection of geography, economics, and politics on a global scale.
Geopolitical Risk - The potential for international affairs to impact a business or country.
Gig Economy - An economy dominated by short-term contracts and freelance work rather than permanent jobs.
Global Governance - Institutions, rules, norms, and legal arrangements to address worldwide issues.
Global Value Chains - Full range of global activities involved in producing a product or service.
Globalization - The process by which businesses and other organizations develop international influence.
Great Power Competition - The rivalry between the world's most powerful nations, notably China and the U.S.
Green Bonds - Bonds that are issued to fund projects that have positive environmental benefits.
Green Finance - Financial investments flowing into sustainable development projects and initiatives.
Green New Deal - A proposed economic stimulus package that aims to address climate change and economic inequality.
Grey Economy - Economic activity that is neither taxed nor monitored by a government; not synonymous with the black market.
Grey Zone Conflict - Activities that are aggressive but remain below the threshold of conventional warfare.
Hard Brexit - A complete break from the European Union without any transitional arrangements.
Helicopter Money - A policy in which a central bank distributes money to the public.
Hybrid Warfare - A mix of conventional warfare, irregular tactics, and cyber warfare.
Hydrocarbon Economy - An economy that relies on hydrocarbon-based fuels like oil, coal, and natural gas.
Hyperglobalization - An extreme form of globalization which sees the world as one huge marketplace.
Import Substitution - An economic policy that emphasizes replacing foreign imports with domestic production.
Inflation Targeting - An economic policy in which a central bank sets a target inflation rate and brings about changes in interest rates to achieve that target.
Information Warfare - The manipulation of information to influence public opinion or obscure the truth.
Isolationism - A policy of remaining apart from the affairs or interests of other groups or countries.
Jobless Growth - Economic growth that does not result in a reduction in unemployment or underemployment.
Junk Bonds - High-risk and high-yield bonds.
Just-in-Time Production - Manufacturing system in which components are delivered immediately before they are required to reduce inventory costs.
Keynesian Economics - Economic theories arguing that government spending can be used to increase total demand and thus increase economic activity.
Kleptocracy - A government with corrupt leaders (kleptocrats) that use power to exploit the people and natural resources to extend their personal wealth.
Knowledge Economy - Economy in which growth is dependent on the quantity, quality, and accessibility of information.
Laissez-faire - An economic philosophy of free-market capitalism that opposes government intervention.
Leveraged Buyout (LBO) - Acquiring a company using a significant amount of borrowed money.
Liberal Order - The post-WWII international system, including international institutions, state cooperation, and the spread of democracy.
Liquidity Trap - A situation in which people hoard money and avoid spending and investment due to economic recession.
Malthusian Trap - A situation where population growth outpaces agricultural production, leading to chronic food shortages.
Market Fundamentalism - A belief in the ability of free markets to solve most problems without government intervention.
Mercantilism - Belief in the benefits of profitable trading and the theory that trade generates wealth.
Minsky Moment - A sudden, severe market collapse after a long period of stability or gradual decline.
Multipolar World - A global system in which power is distributed among more than two nations.
Narco-state - A political and economic term applied to countries where all legitimate institutions become penetrated by the power and wealth of the illegal drug trade.
Nationalism - Advocacy for the interests of one's own nation, especially to the exclusion of others.
